blogs.title: When Expert Testimony Defies Physics: The Substantial Evidence Standard in Patent Infringement
blogs.description: Analyzing the Federal Circuit's reversal of the '134 patent infringement verdict, this post examines how contradictory expert testimony regarding signal sampling timelines failed the substantial evidence test. It highlights the court's scrutiny of expert opinions that rely on physically impossible mappings and the implications for litigators preparing infringement evidence.

blogs.title: Prosecution History Disavowal: Did Amending 'Two or Three' to 'Three' Surrender Claim Scope?
blogs.description: Focusing on the '775 patent, this post explores the court's rejection of the argument that amending claims from 'two or three signals' to 'three signals' constituted a clear and unambiguous disavowal of two-signal devices. It discusses the high threshold for prosecution history estoppel and claim construction based on amendment history.

blogs.title: The Burden of Proof for Algorithmic Claims: Mapping Specific Multiplications to Accused Devices
blogs.description: This post dissects the infringement analysis for the '775 patent's 'seven multiplications' limitation, illustrating the rigorous requirement to prove every specific mathematical operation claimed. It offers insights into the challenges of proving literal infringement in software and radio algorithm patents where general functionality is insufficient.
